content: Approximately 1% of the maternal dose of this drug is transferred to breast milk. However, there is limited information available regarding the effects of this medication on breastfed infants. Combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs) may reduce milk production in breastfeeding women. This reduction in milk supply can occur at any time but is less likely once breastfeeding is well-established. When feasible, breastfeeding women should be advised to use alternative methods of contraception until they have discontinued breastfeeding. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be carefully weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the medication and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child, whether from the medication itself or from the underlying maternal condition. Regarding safety during pregnancy, this medication is generally considered acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated evidence of fetal risk. The pharmacokinetics of the drug include hepatic metabolism, with two inactive acid metabolites of drospirenone (DSRP). The half-life of ethinyl estradiol is approximately 24 hours, while the half-life of drospirenone is about 30 hours. The drug is excreted primarily through urine (38–47% as inactive metabolites) and feces (17–20% as inactive metabolites).
